text:
maya: Quick heads-up — product is proposing we flip the default for the /v1/generate `strict_response` flag from `false` -> `true` on 2026-04-20 to reduce hallucinations for higher-safety customers. This is potentially breaking for integrations that relied on permissive outputs. Who can help scope impact (API behavior, SDKs, docs, deprecation comms)? cc @kevin @sara

kevin: I can run a quick compatibility sweep. Two quick Qs: will this be a server-side default change only (no param renaming), and do we have a header-based opt-out plan?

maya: server-side only (no param rename) — clients can still send `strict_response=false` to keep legacy behavior. Product wants to avoid adding a new param name. They asked if we can support an Accept-Version header instead for gradual rollout.

sara: If clients can pass `strict_response` explicitly then it's not strictly breaking, but SDKs that don't expose that flag will change behavior. We need to update all official SDKs (py/ts/go) and publish a minor release before the flip. Also show an env var opt-out for Redwood Dedicated / Private docs.

jack: Agree with SDK work. Suggest timeline: announce 2 weeks, update SDKs + integration tests in week 1, canary flip for 5% traffic week 2, full flip week 3. Also need a fallback circuit (model-pin fallback) if error rates spike.

anna: (product) We prefer a 30-day public deprecation window. Suggested comms: blog post + notice in Console + email to customers with >$500/mo spend. Also add a compatibility header option `Accept-Api-Version: 2026-04-strict` so customers can pin behavior without changing request body.

kevin: Implementation notes for eng-platform: we can support header negotiation in the routing layer. Pseudocode for header check:

```
if req.headers['Accept-Api-Version'] contains 'strict' -> default_strict = true
else default_strict = server_default (false until flip date)
// explicit body param `strict_response` overrides header
```

sara: Good. For SDKs: expose `strict_response` on client constructors as well as per-call override, and add a `default_strict` option when initializing client. We'll bump minor versions: py 1.14.0, js 2.7.0, go 0.9.0.

deploy-bot: Deploy window note: planned server change scheduled for 2026-04-20 03:00 UTC. Will do canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with health checks.

maya: Can someone add a checklist in the PR for rollout? Things I want: (1) SDK releases linked, (2) docs page updated, (3) Console banner draft, (4) email list + blog draft, (5) monitoring dashboard (error rate, latency, fallback rate), (6) rollback playbook.

kevin: I'll open the eng-platform PR and add the checklist. Will add a feature flag gated by date and a runtime flag `features.strict_default_v2` so we can toggle without deploy.

jack: For monitoring: create a panel showing "calls with implicit strict_response" (requests that didn't set param but were affected), and alert if user-facing error rate > 0.5% or latency P95 increases > 30%. Also track number of clients using Accept-Api-Version header.

docs-bot: Draft docs section added: https://docs.redwood.ai/guides/compatibility/strict-response (WIP). Will post PR link when ready.

maya: Awesome. Final Q: do we want to treat this as a breaking change in API changelog or as a behavioral default change (non-breaking because flag exists)? Product prefers non-breaking but we'll still run the 30-day notice. Any objections?

sara: Technically non-breaking because explicit param preserves behavior, but practically it's a behavioral change — mark clearly in changelog and release notes.

anna: No objections. Proceed with the 30-day communications plan.

kevin: I'll tag SDK owners and start the compatibility tests. PR: eng-platform#4321 (WIP).

maya: Thanks all — I'll coordinate the comms and post the timeline in the RFC doc. :thumbsup:

jack: leaving a small checklist here for reviewer: run `make sdk-integration-test`, verify `strict_response` present in samples, smoke test canary by setting `Accept-Api-Version` header locally.

maya: Example curl for QA (feel free to paste into integration tests):

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept-Api-Version: 2026-04-strict" \
  -d '{"prompt":"Explain binary search","strict_response":true}'
```

kevin: Copying that into the PR. Will add a small shim in the JS SDK to set header when `client.defaultStrict = true` so apps can opt-in without changing calls.

maya: Great. I'll drop a calendar invite for a short sync next Wed to confirm go/no-go after canary metrics.

[end of thread]
